entries.title: Five fixes: dashboard chart axes, missing-report notice, title-slide badges, slides overlay hint, and File field accessibility
entries.summary: Five bugs corrected in one sweep: (1) Bar, line, area, and scatter chart y-axes now size to the longest tick label, so values like "600" no longer render as "00". (2) Opening a report workbench URL with an invalid or deleted query ID now shows an inline notice ("This report could not be found…") instead of a raw "Request failed" toast. (3) When a session has two title slides, each **Files** tab row now shows its own freshness badge instead of both showing the first slide's state. (4) The **Overlay** hint in the Slides designer now correctly states that the overlay tints with the background colour (not "darkens the photo"). (5) The upload button in a **File** field now receives the field's `id` and `aria-invalid` attribute, so screen readers and validation alerts link correctly to the control.

where.path: Dashboards → any bar/line/area/scatter widget; Reports → Workbench; Sessions → session → Files tab; Marketing → Slides → designer → Overlay; Contacts → Add Contact → File field

entries.use_case: Organizers who rely on dashboards with counts over 99, manage multiple title slides per session, or use the Slides designer will see accurate data and labels without workarounds. Teams using assistive technology or browser-based accessibility audits on contact forms will now get correct error linking on File fields.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports truncated y-axis labels on charts, a confusing 'Request failed' error on reports, mismatched title-slide badges, or accessibility audit failures on File fields.
internal.gotchas: The missing-report notice suppresses the toast and does not retry 404/400 responses; a failed background refetch keeps the previously loaded report intact so edits are not lost.
internal.talk_track: Five QA fixes shipped together: chart axes now scale to any number of digits; a bad report URL shows a friendly inline message; two title slides on one session each show their own status; the Slides overlay hint is accurate; and File field errors are properly linked for screen readers.

draft.docs_gap: The dashboards guide should note that value-axis width adjusts automatically to the longest tick label. The report-builder guide should document the inline error notice shown when a saved report cannot be found. The Slides guide should clarify that the overlay tints with the background colour rather than darkening the photo.

entries.title: Scheduled report links and sends now respect "Hide personal details"
entries.summary: When a saved report has **Hide personal details** turned on, the **View Report Online** link and every scheduled email delivery now mask names and email addresses. Previously, the scheduled path always sent unmasked data regardless of the report setting.

where.path: Reports → saved report → Scheduled tab → View Report Online link / scheduled email delivery

entries.use_case: Organizations that share scheduled reports with stakeholders who should not see speaker PII (names, emails) can now rely on the report's own privacy setting being honoured in every delivery, not just in the interactive view.

cs_action.note: Any customer who had a scheduled report with Hide personal details enabled was receiving unmasked data. No active schedules were running against masked reports at the time of the fix (0 found in US and EU), but worth confirming with affected accounts.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why their scheduled report link or email shows full names and emails even though the report is set to hide personal details.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using scheduled reports on a masked saved report.
internal.gotchas: The fix reads the saved report's Hide personal details flag. If the schedule was created before the flag was set on the report, the next send will now correctly mask. No retroactive re-send occurs.
internal.talk_track: The scheduled report link and email now always match what you see in the interactive report — if Hide personal details is on, every delivery respects it.

entries.title: Awards round names, import validation, and file-download copy fixes
entries.summary: Four user-visible corrections ship together. (1) **Awards → Rounds**: round names and scorecard question labels containing `<` or `>` now display exactly as typed instead of showing `<` / `>`. (2) **Awards → Submissions → Import**: rows with a non-http(s) URL (e.g. `ftp://…`) in a URL question now fail with a clear reason ("URL expects a valid http(s) URL … was not imported.") instead of silently clearing the stored value. (3) **Awards → Submissions → Import** for self-nomination programs: the import template no longer lists Nominee columns that the form already hides and fills automatically. (4) **Approvals → Files**: a file approved but held under a future release time now returns "This file is not released yet and cannot be downloaded." on a public download attempt instead of "waiting on approval".

where.path: Awards → Program → Rounds / Submissions → Import; Approvals → Files

entries.use_case: Teams managing awards programs can now trust that round names with special characters display correctly, that bad URLs in bulk imports are caught and reported before any data is changed, and that self-nomination import templates only ask for the columns submitters actually need to fill.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports garbled round names, a confusing import result for URL fields, extra nominee columns in a self-nomination import, or a misleading error message on a held-but-approved file download.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Awards with rounds, bulk imports, or file approvals with release times.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Program → Rounds (angle-bracket names); Awards → Submissions → Import (URL / self-nomination); Approvals → Files (embargoed download message)
internal.gotchas: Existing rows in US prod with encoded round names (2 rounds + 1 label) heal on read — no backfill needed. EU had no affected rows.
internal.talk_track: These are four quiet correctness fixes: round names now render as typed, bad URLs in imports are rejected with a clear message before touching stored data, self-nomination imports no longer ask for nominee columns, and the error message on a held file now accurately says the file is not released yet.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that round names and scorecard labels support angle-bracket characters, that URL fields in imports require http(s) and will fail the row with a reason if the value is invalid, and that self-nomination program import templates omit nominee columns.

entries.title: Five Disclosures fixes: inline CFP section, thank-you page, Mitigations tab, form permissions, and request source label
entries.summary: Five bugs in the Disclosures feature are resolved. **Inline submitter disclosure** on a CFP form now renders correctly and no longer blocks submission with a 400 error — the disclosure section appears under **Participants** (or under **Session** for linked-entry forms) and must be completed before the form can be submitted. The **completed disclosure thank-you page** now names the organisation that holds the disclosure instead of "Sessionboard". The **Mitigations** tab is hidden when the org's Credits feature is off, and its 403 error message now correctly asks for the **Credits** permission rather than the Disclosures permission. The **New form** button on the **Forms** tab is hidden from users who lack the Disclosures permission, and a permission-denied create attempt now shows a clear message instead of raw API text. Disclosure requests sent from the **Requests** tab picker are now labelled **Sent manually** instead of "Sent from profile".

where.path: Disclosures → Forms / Requests / Mitigations; CFP submission form → Participants

entries.use_case: Organisations running accredited events that require inline disclosures on their CFP can now collect submitter disclosures without the form silently failing. Admins with limited roles also see accurate permission prompts and correctly scoped UI controls throughout the Disclosures module.

cs_action.note: The inline CFP disclosure fix (SB-10345) unblocks SB-9795. Customers who reported that the disclosure section never appeared on their CFP form should be re-tested against prod after this ships. The Mitigations tab now requires both lessons_credits AND credits org features; orgs with only lessons_credits will lose the tab.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that submitters cannot complete a CFP form when inline disclosures are enabled, or that the Mitigations tab shows a confusing permission error.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Disclosures with a CFP form that has 'Ask the submitter inline' enabled, or any org where the Mitigations tab was showing a misleading error.
internal.staff_path: Org or Event → Disclosures → Forms / Requests / Mitigations
internal.gotchas: Orgs with lessons_credits on but credits off will no longer see the Mitigations tab — this is correct behaviour but may surprise customers who previously navigated there. After a server-side disclosure refusal the section becomes visible but does not block Continue; the server re-validates on the next submit.
internal.talk_track: The inline disclosure section on CFP forms now works end-to-end: it appears for the submitter, must be answered before submission, and the server validates it correctly. The Mitigations tab and permission messages are also more accurate.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the inline submitter disclosure flow on CFP forms — specifically that the section appears under Participants (or Session for linked-entry forms), what happens after a server refusal, and that both the org Credits feature and Credits permission are required for the Mitigations tab.
draft.why_use_it: Disclosures let you collect and track conflict-of-interest declarations from speakers, submitters, and other participants as part of your accreditation workflow. You can send requests automatically, collect answers inline on submission forms, and export results for your accreditor — all without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Completed and expired disclosure links now show the sending organisation's name
entries.summary: When a speaker or contact reopens a disclosure link that has already been completed or has expired, the page now names the organisation (and event, where applicable) that sent the request — for example, "**Acme Conference** has your disclosure on file" and "sent to you by **Acme Conference**" — instead of crediting "Sessionboard".

where.path: Disclosure link → completed or expired state page

entries.use_case: When a speaker clicks an old disclosure link after already submitting, they now see the correct organisation name on the confirmation screen, which removes confusion about who collected their disclosure and reinforces trust in the process.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that completed disclosure links showed 'Sessionboard' instead of their org name.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Disclosures (beta) feature.
internal.gotchas: Revoked and unknown/invalid tokens still return a 404 with no org information — only completed and expired links are affected by this fix.
internal.talk_track: Speakers who reopen a completed disclosure link will now see your organisation's name and logo on the confirmation screen, not 'Sessionboard'.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that completed and expired disclosure links display the sending organisation's name and logo, and clarify that revoked links remain anonymous (404).
draft.why_use_it: Disclosures let you collect conflict-of-interest declarations from speakers and participants before your event. Requests are sent by email and completed through a secure, token-based link. Once a person submits, the link stays accessible so they can confirm their disclosure is on file, and the page always identifies your organisation as the sender.

entries.title: Team Lead and CFP builder: track creation, form settings, speaker questions and campaign type now work reliably
entries.summary: Four bugs in the AI agent workflows are resolved. **Ask → Team Lead**: approving an "Add tracks to this event" card now actually creates the tracks (previously every approval silently failed). The **Get session form** tool no longer returns the entire field library, so Team Lead can read form settings, identify the acting user, and apply notification and submission-limit changes in a single conversation. Adding a **Speaker bio** question to a CFP form no longer places a duplicate row when the field already exists under a different scope label. **Ask → Email Campaigns**: creating a Sessions-type campaign draft now saves correctly — previously the `audience_type` and `schedule_intent` metadata keys were rejected by validation, causing the draft to fall back to a People audience silently.
entries.use_case: Organizers using Ask to build or update a CFP form — adding tracks, setting submission limits, assigning notification recipients, or creating a Sessions email campaign — can now complete those tasks in a single approved conversation without silent failures or duplicate fields.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Ask approved a track card but nothing appeared, that Team Lead couldn't identify who 'me' is on a form, that a Speaker bio question was duplicated, or that a Sessions campaign draft saved as People.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Ask / Team Lead for CFP form setup or email campaign creation.
internal.gotchas: All four fixes require both this API PR and agents#160 to be deployed; either can go first. Seventeen duplicate 'Speaker bio' rows exist on QA events (5881 and clones 7074–7172) in US prod — no backfill is planned. The track-creation fix also covers create_session, duplicate_sessions, delete_sessions, and update_submission_status tools which had the same missing eventId gap since SB-8019.
internal.talk_track: If a customer says Ask approved a card but nothing changed, or their Sessions campaign saved as People, these four fixes address the root causes — the agent now correctly receives the event context and the campaign metadata schema accepts the audience and schedule fields Ask sends.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document what Team Lead can do with CFP forms (add tracks, set submission limits, configure notifications, add speaker questions) and note that Ask handles Sessions campaign creation including audience type selection.
draft.why_use_it: Team Lead lets you build and update call-for-papers forms, program tracks, and email campaigns by describing what you want in plain language. Approve the cards it proposes and the changes are applied directly to your event — no manual navigation through multiple settings screens required.

entries.title: Five fixes for clips, media editor, and transcriptions
entries.summary: Five bugs in the Marketing clips, media editor, and transcriptions surfaces are resolved: (1) Animated captions in exported MP4s now appear bottom-centre (matching the preview) instead of top-left. (2) **Export edited video** and the transcript **Clip** button now correctly include the animated caption style chosen in **Preview options**; when a cut is present, a toast explains why standard captions are used instead. (3) Uploading a non-audio file (e.g. a PNG) as **background audio** now shows an error toast listing the accepted formats (MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV, OGG) and blocks the upload. (4) The **Clips** library now pages through all clips with a **Load more** button and a "Showing N of M clips" count, removing the previous hard cap of 100. (5) The "Transcribed from N highlighted moments Goldcast clipped" note on the **Transcript** tab now appears only on Goldcast-imported recordings, not on uploaded .srt/.vtt files.
entries.use_case: Teams producing post-event video clips can now trust that animated captions land where they appear in the preview, that every export path honours the caption style they chose, and that the clips library shows their full archive rather than stopping at 100.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that exported clips have captions in the wrong position, that animated captions are missing from exports, that the clips library seems to be missing older clips, or that a Goldcast note appears on uploaded transcripts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Marketing clips, the media editor, or transcriptions — particularly those who have more than 100 clips or who use animated captions.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → Edit & clip → Preview options / Export edited video; Marketing → Clips
internal.gotchas: Animated captions are silently downgraded to standard captions when the clip contains cuts (splices); the editor shows an info toast explaining this. The Remotion worker must be on the latest bundle (deployed with this UI release) for the caption-position fix to take effect.
internal.talk_track: Exported clips now match the preview exactly for caption position and style. The clips library pages through your full archive with Load more, and the Goldcast transcript note only appears on Goldcast recordings.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should note the "Showing N of M clips" count and the Load more button, and the Media editor section should document the animated-captions limitation when a clip contains cuts.

entries.title: Clip exports from WebM recordings now succeed, Topic filter includes tracks and tags, and animated clips render with accurate colours
entries.summary: Four fixes to the **Marketing → Media** clips workflow ship together. (1) **WebM recordings** can now be trimmed and exported as clips — the worker detects VP8/VP9/Opus codecs and transcodes to H.264/AAC automatically; clips longer than 10 minutes from a WebM source show a clear "Export failed" reason instead of silently failing. (2) The **Topic** filter in **Media → Clips** now lists and matches session Tracks and Tags in addition to taxonomy topics, so clips are findable by the labels already on their sessions. (3) Animated clip renders no longer appear darker or more saturated than the source; the output is tagged BT.709 so players decode colours correctly. (4) Exporting a splice (multiple cut segments) that also carries a logo, text insert, or audio insert now returns a clear 400 error ("Logos, text and audio inserts can't be added to a video with cuts yet…") instead of silently dropping the overlay from the rendered clip.
entries.use_case: Teams that recorded sessions as WebM files (common with browser-based capture tools) can now export trimmed clips without manual conversion. Organizers who tag sessions with tracks or custom tags can filter the clips library by those same labels to find content quickly.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that clip exports from WebM recordings always fail, that the Topic filter shows no options, or that animated clips look washed out or too dark.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Marketing Clips, especially those whose AV or virtual platform produces WebM recordings.
internal.gotchas: WebM clips longer than 10 minutes that require transcoding (VP8/VP9/Opus codecs) will fail with an explicit error message — this is intentional and by design, not a bug. Clips from WebM sources whose codecs are already mp4-compatible (e.g. AV1 with no audio) still stream-copy at any length. The splice-with-overlay change is a breaking API behaviour change: requests that previously returned 201 (but rendered incorrectly) now return 400.
internal.talk_track: If your recordings come from a browser-based tool and clips were always failing, that's fixed — the system now detects the codec and converts automatically. The Topic filter in the clips library now picks up the tracks and tags already on your sessions, so you don't need separate taxonomy entries to filter content.

draft.docs_gap: The Clips guide should document the 10-minute transcoding cap for WebM sources, the expanded Topic filter behaviour (tracks + tags), and the splice-with-overlay validation error.
draft.why_use_it: Clips lets you turn any section of a recorded session into a shareable video asset — trimmed, branded, and optionally animated — without leaving Sessionboard. Use it to produce speaker highlight reels, social snippets, or on-demand previews directly from your event recordings, then share or embed them wherever your audience is.

entries.title: My Contracts: "Needs Signature" tab now reflects each signer's own status
entries.summary: The **Needs Signature** tab in the portal's **My Contracts** section now shows only contracts that still need *your* signature. Once you have signed, the contract moves out of **Needs Signature** and the **Sign now** button is hidden; the row badge reads **Waiting on others** until all signers are done. Previously, Sessionboard e-sign contracts stayed in **Needs Signature** for everyone until the final countersigner acted, because the tab used the overall contract status rather than each person's signing state.
entries.use_case: Signers who have already completed their part of a Sessionboard e-sign contract no longer see it cluttering their Needs Signature list, reducing confusion and unnecessary follow-up with event staff.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that speakers or participants say they already signed but the contract still appears under Needs Signature in their portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessionboard e-sign contracts with multiple signers (e.g. speaker + countersigner).
internal.gotchas: Fix applies only to Sessionboard e-sign contracts; DocuSign contracts and uploaded contracts are unchanged. If the API has not yet been updated to the version that returns needsMySignature, the portal falls back to the old status-based rule — deploy the API half (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4711) first or simultaneously.
internal.talk_track: After a speaker signs their portion of a contract, it immediately leaves their Needs Signature tab and shows Waiting on others — they won't keep asking if something went wrong with their signature.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the Needs Signature tab is per-signer and that the "Waiting on others" badge appears once the portal user has signed but other signers have not yet completed the contract.

entries.title: Four contract fixes: account name in templates, read-only template access, portal Needs Signature accuracy, and return link after signing
entries.summary: Four bugs in the Contracts workflow are resolved: (1) Account company names were blank in native e-sign contracts and previews — they now resolve correctly from the account's field values. (2) Users with **Can view contracts** permission could not open the **Templates** tab ("Could not load templates") — listing and previewing templates now requires only read access. (3) In the portal **My Contracts** view, a contract the signer had already signed continued to appear under **Needs Signature** while waiting on a countersigner — the tab, badge, and init count now reflect each signer's own status. (4) After signing from the portal **Sign now** link, signers were left on the /sign page with no way back — the signing page now shows a **Back to My Contracts** link and redirects to **My Contracts** with a "Contract signed" confirmation after signing.
entries.use_case: Teams sending native e-sign contracts to sponsors or speakers can trust that the company name appears correctly in the document, read-only team members can browse and preview templates without hitting an error, and signers get a smooth return to their portal after signing instead of being stranded on the signing page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports blank company names in account contracts, a read-only user hitting a 403 on Templates, a signer seeing a contract they already signed still under Needs Signature, or a signer left stranded after signing from the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using native Sessionboard e-sign contracts, especially those with account-subject contracts (sponsors) or multi-signer sequential workflows.
internal.staff_path: Org → Contracts → Templates; portal My Contracts → Needs Signature tab
internal.gotchas: The return-URL security uses an HMAC tied to the signing token — a tampered return param is silently ignored and no back link is shown. DocuSign and uploaded contracts keep the old status-based Needs Signature rule (single recipient). Emailed signing links do not include a return link.
internal.talk_track: We fixed four contract issues in one sweep: account names now appear in documents, read-only users can browse templates, the Needs Signature count is per-signer not per-contract, and signers land back in My Contracts after signing.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note that the portal Needs Signature tab reflects each individual signer's own status (not the overall contract status), and that the portal Sign now flow returns signers to My Contracts after completion.

entries.title: Six fixes: CFP draft reset 403 error, "Refunded" acceptance-fee status, spurious connection-error toast, focus management after removal, contract editor badge wrapping, and video editor accessibility
entries.summary: Six bugs corrected in one sweep: (1) After using **Reset saved data** on a CFP draft, the next **Submit** no longer returns a 403 "Found non-existing or deleted Session" error — the deleted draft is removed from the cache and the submission sends with `sessionId: null`. (2) The **Connections** status column now shows **Refunded** (with date and amount) when an acceptance fee has been refunded, in English, German, Spanish, and French. (3) Navigating **Quick Launch → Continue → Back** no longer flashes a red "Connection error … signal is aborted" toast for cancelled in-flight requests; real network failures still toast. (4) After confirming a removal, keyboard focus returns to **Apply filter** instead of jumping to "Skip to main content". (5) At 1440 px with the Ask panel open, the contract template editor's Draft/module badges no longer wrap into a three-line chip. (6) The caption-style select and aspect-ratio select in the video editor now have accessible names readable by screen readers.

where.path: Sessions → submission form (CFP draft reset → Submit); Speakers → Connections (acceptance fee status); Quick Launch → Continue → Back; Marketing → Create (removal confirm); Contracts → template editor; Marketing → Media → video editor

entries.use_case: Organizers running a CFP can now safely reset a draft and resubmit without hitting a 403 error. Teams reviewing acceptance fees get accurate refund status in their language, and keyboard-only users and screen-reader users encounter fewer focus and labelling issues across the platform.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports a 403 error after resetting a CFP draft, a missing 'Refunded' status on acceptance fees, a spurious 'Connection error' toast during Quick Launch navigation, focus jumping to 'Skip to main content' after a removal, badge wrapping in the contract editor, or accessibility audit failures on the video editor selects.
internal.gotchas: The abort-error suppression only silences React Query's own AbortError on caller-cancelled requests; genuine network failures still produce the toast. The CFP draft reset fix drops the row from the in-progress cache and refetches both queries, so a race between reset and submit should no longer be possible.
internal.talk_track: Six QA fixes shipped together: resetting a CFP draft and resubmitting now works cleanly; refunded acceptance fees show the correct status with date and amount in four languages; Quick Launch back-navigation no longer shows a false connection-error toast; keyboard focus lands in the right place after a removal confirm; contract editor badges stay on one line at 1440 px; and the video editor caption-style and aspect-ratio controls are now labelled for screen readers.

draft.docs_gap: The submission-forms guide should note that resetting a saved draft fully clears the cached draft IDs before the next submission. The speaker-acceptance guide should document the Refunded status (with date and amount) that appears in the Connections column when an acceptance fee is reversed.

entries.title: Four fixes for CFP acceptance payments: correct field names in error messages, pay-link emails reach only the payer, no retroactive billing, and refunded payments show the right status
entries.summary: Four bugs in the CFP acceptance-payment flow are corrected: (1) Length-limit validation errors on draft/submit now show the field's configured alias (e.g. **Business Mobile**) instead of the base field name. (2) Payment-link merge tags in acceptance emails are sent only to the contact who can pay; when **Combine recipients per record** would deliver one copy to multiple people, the payment tags render empty to prevent the wrong person receiving a pay link. (3) Acceptance payments are never billed retroactively — only sessions accepted after the payment feature was activated on a form are charged. (4) A refunded acceptance payment now shows as **Refunded** (not **Paid**), and the pay and complete-free actions refuse to act on it.

where.path: Sessions → submission form → Acceptance settings; Communications → email merge tags for acceptance payments

entries.use_case: Organizers collecting payments on session acceptance can trust that pay links go only to the person responsible for payment, that speakers accepted before the payment feature was turned on are not billed unexpectedly, and that refunded rows are clearly labelled so finance reconciliation is accurate.

cs_action.note: US replica shows 566 sessions where the submitter contact (not the payer) previously received a broken pay link; EU shows 38. Those speakers got a link that errored. Also 15 refunded CFP payment rows in US now show Refunded instead of Paid — flag to any customer reconciling payments. A db:migrate is required at deploy time (migration: 20261027100000-cfp-forms-acceptance-payment-enabled-at).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that acceptance payment emails went to the wrong person, that speakers accepted before the feature was enabled are being billed, or that a refunded payment still shows as Paid.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using on-acceptance CFP payments — particularly those with co-speaker submissions or who have recently refunded acceptance payments.
internal.gotchas: The activation timestamp (acceptance_payment_enabled_at) is stamped at deploy via migration for forms already set to on_acceptance; cloned events get the clone time. Bulk re-saves skip sessions already accepted before that timestamp. The one-person guard on pay-link tags counts distinct To, CC, BCC, and additional-contact addresses — not just To.
internal.talk_track: Four QA fixes for CFP acceptance payments: field alias names now appear correctly in validation errors; pay links in acceptance emails go only to the payer (co-speakers no longer receive a link that errors); sessions accepted before the payment feature was activated are not billed retroactively; and refunded payments are clearly labelled Refunded so your finance team can reconcile accurately.

draft.docs_gap: The accept-or-decline guide should document how acceptance payments work, including the activation timestamp behaviour, the one-payer-only rule for merge tags, and the Refunded status on invoices.

entries.title: Seven fixes: award category crash, field-translation numbers, notification links, PDF viewer on iOS Safari, booklet pagination, preload recovery, and Ready Room error noise
entries.summary: Seven bugs corrected in one sweep: (1) Award submissions with no category no longer crash the **Details** tab — they now show **No category** in English, German, Spanish, and French. (2) Custom field translation values that are numbers or booleans no longer throw an error in the **Field Translations** sidebar; they are coerced to strings, and objects are treated as empty. (3) File-export notification links that point to an external domain now open in a new tab instead of crashing the router. (4) The PDF viewer and floor-map PDF picker now load the legacy PDF.js build on iOS 15–18 Safari, where the modern build was missing a required `Map` method and failing silently. (5) Booklet preview pagination no longer throws when the preview iframe detaches from the document. (6) The Vite preload-error recovery now reloads the page correctly every time a chunk fails to load, instead of getting stuck after the first reload and leaving imports undefined. (7) Ready Room API calls no longer report 401, 404, and 422 responses to Sentry as errors; only 5xx and network failures are tracked, so callers still receive the error.

where.path: Awards → submission → Details tab; Sessions → Field Translations sidebar; Notifications bell → file-export link; Poster Gallery → PDF viewer; Floor Maps → PDF picker; Marketing → Print → Booklet preview; Ready Room

entries.use_case: Organizers reviewing uncategorized award submissions, translating custom fields with numeric values, or working with PDF content on iOS devices will no longer hit crashes or blank screens. Teams using file-export notifications or booklet previews will see those surfaces work reliably without workarounds.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports a crash on the Awards Details tab for uncategorized submissions, errors in the Field Translations sidebar, broken notification links for file exports, PDF viewer failures on iOS Safari, booklet preview issues, or repeated page-blank errors after a deploy.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — all fixes are default-on.
internal.gotchas: The Ready Room change suppresses Sentry noise for 401/404/422 but does not change how callers handle those errors — speakers and organizers still see the appropriate error states. The iOS PDF fix loads the legacy pdfjs build only; modern browsers are unaffected.
internal.talk_track: Seven QA fixes shipped together: uncategorized award submissions now show 'No category' instead of crashing; numeric custom-field translation values no longer break the sidebar; file-export notification links open correctly in a new tab; the PDF viewer works on iOS 15–18 Safari; booklet previews no longer fail when the iframe detaches; the preload-error recovery reloads reliably on every chunk failure; and Ready Room API noise in error tracking is reduced to genuine failures only.

draft.docs_gap: The awards guide should note that submissions without a category display "No category" on the Details tab. The language-variants guide should clarify that numeric and boolean custom-field values are accepted in the Field Translations sidebar. The notifications guide should note that file-export links to external domains open in a new tab.
